change_class_rationale: Adds an executable oya-dev-cli governance gate plus tests, manifest-index materiality metadata, and report evidence; no production runtime behavior, tenant data path, public API, UI, or external dependency changed.
task: FD-001 serialized manifest/workspace alignment gate after PR #148 merged planning closure and CI governance gates.

findings: CLI tests prove strict failure on missing manifest crates, clean success, FD-001 material filtering from fd001_material flags, --all-manifests expansion, repeated --manifest aggregation, mixed-scope rejection, index/manifest identity mismatch rejection, empty-crate rejection, required report evidence, evidence path confinement, and per-manifest required/present/missing arrays.
Live FD-001 material scan is intentionally red in strict mode: 8 manifests, 333 required crates, 333 exact workspace crates missing.
TDD regression suite covers the high/medium adversarial findings and keeps report-only mode from becoming a silent green.
Gate remains an oya-dev-cli validation lane and does not add runtime product dependencies or mutate product service code.
FD-001 materiality moved into specs/microservices/manifests-index.json so default scope is machine-readable instead of hidden in gate code.

CLI contract is explicit: --report-only requires --emit-report, --emit-report is repo-relative under evidence/, --all-manifests cannot mix with explicit --manifest paths, and manifest-index rows are bound to manifest.microservice.

cargo fmt --check, cargo check -p oya-dev-cli --locked, cargo clippy -p oya-dev-cli --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, targeted CLI tests, planning-closure gate, planning-closure tests, and JSON parse checks passed.
Report evidence now includes required_crates, present_crates, missing_crates, expected_microservice, and manifest path per scanned manifest for reviewer-auditable reconciliation.
No secrets, credentials, tenant data, network calls, production deploy paths, auth flows, or external services are touched; report writes are constrained under evidence/.
Gate performs bounded JSON scans over manifest-index rows and workspace Cargo.toml members; no hot-path runtime code changed.
Implementation reuses existing workspace member/package helpers and keeps the new validation lane isolated in one module with CLI dispatch wiring.
Change is isolated to one CLI gate, its dispatch/usage wiring, tests, manifest-index metadata, and evidence output; rollback is a narrow file-level revert.
Machine-readable evidence is emitted at evidence/fd001/manifest-workspace-alignment-2026-05-19.json and multispectrum evidence is maintained for the changeset.

Fresh-context adversarial findings were reconciled: hardcoded material scope replaced by fd001_material metadata, index identity binding added, report-only evidence required, empty declarations rejected, audit arrays emitted, coverage expanded, and report paths confined.
Implements the master-plan fanout rule mechanically: product write lanes remain blocked until manifest/workspace alignment is made explicit and verified.

source_driven_notes: No new external dependency or frontend framework was introduced.
JSON traversal uses serde_json::Value object/array/string accessors; docs.rs documents Value as representing any valid JSON value and get/as_* accessors returning Option for type/key mismatches.
Workspace/package parsing reuses existing oya-dev-cli workspace_manifest helpers instead of adding a TOML dependency or second parser.
remaining_risks: This slice does not create the 333 missing FD-001 exact workspace crates; it makes that blocker mechanically visible and reportable.
Strict gate is not wired into run-all/required CI yet; that should happen after the reconciliation strategy is selected to avoid deliberately red required contexts.
